subject: SLA decision worksheet: hosted vs incumbent
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@novara.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: SLA decision worksheet: hosted vs incumbent

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the SLA decision worksheet. I captured the items we discussed related to end-to-end latency qualification, throughput and streaming behavior. Please flag anything I missed.

Call summary (short):
- Business ask: Novara needs predictable latency for user-facing clinical assistant flows (live chat, short prompts) and an escalation-free migration path from the incumbent provider.
- Primary targets discussed: p95 and p99 end-to-end (client -> our API -> model -> response). You indicated target ranges rather than hard limits: p95 in the 120–250 ms envelope and p99 up to ~700 ms depending on payload/streaming characteristics.

What Redwood captured and proposes as acceptance criteria (initial worksheet):
1) Baseline traffic profile (we need replay logs):
   - 50% streaming chat sessions (avg token rate 15 t/s, user RTT target ~200–400ms for partial frames)
   - 35% single-turn generation (median 60 tokens)
   - 15% embeddings/batch jobs (background)
2) Throughput/concurrency assumptions:
   - Steady concurrency target: 80 concurrent chat sessions (sustained during business hours)
   - Burst capacity: short bursts to 300 concurrent sessions for 3–5 minutes
3) Acceptance thresholds (POC stage):
   - p95 end-to-end <= 180 ms for single-turn generation at steady concurrency
   - p99 end-to-end <= 650 ms for mixed traffic during sustained bursts
   - Streaming partials: first token to client (<150 ms) for 95% of streaming sessions
4) Test plan highlights:
   - Provide a 24–72 hour production replay (anonymized) or a representative traffic trace — we'll run a staged replay against hosted and the incumbent configuration in parallel.
   - Run three test modes: baseline (steady), burst (sustained 30 min at 200 conc), and cold-start (24 hr idle then spike).
   - Measure both server-side token latencies and full e2e client-observed times (Jarvis agent)

Attachments: I drafted an acceptance matrix (redwood-sla-acceptance-matrix-v1.csv) that maps test mode to pass/fail criteria and required artifacts. I uploaded it to the shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Novara/SLA-worksheet.

Asks from your side (items we need to proceed):
- Agree on the traffic profile above OR share replay logs (preferred)
- Confirm which model(s) you want tested (incumbent model name + quantization/version)
- Point person for procurement/POC logistics (ProcureOps seems likely)

Proposed next steps and timeline
- Elena: share replay data and confirm model names by Fri Dec 4
- Redwood: spin up parallel runs (hosted vs incumbent) and deliver initial benchmark report within 7 business days of receiving data
- Quick sync 30 min after initial report to decide go/no-go and next acceptance thresholds

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering based on the logs you share.

—
Jordan Blake
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0149

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and the worksheet. Quick answers inline: 

- Traffic profile: that breakdown looks right for us. I can share a 48-hour anonymized replay (we redact PHI) — ProcureOps will push it to your S3 bucket. Expect that by EOD Thu Dec 3.
- Models: incumbent is "MedPrompt-XL v2.1" (quantized) and we want Redwood to test against Redwood-rc1 (recommended) plus a higher-compression variant for cost comparison.
- Warm-up/KV cache: our live chat flows tend to open multiple short-lived sessions for clinicians; cold-starts are common at shift changes. We want to see explicit cold-start and cache-warmed runs.

One clarification: for streaming partials you wrote ~150 ms — our product team would be satisfied with 200 ms for the first partial as long as subsequent partials are consistent. Is that reasonable?

ProcureOps (cc) — please confirm you’ll drop the replay to the S3 path Jordan mentioned.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Fwd: internal - quick benchmark notes (RC1 baseline)

Forwarding internal bench notes after running a quick RC1 vs incumbent micro-probe using the Novara-like profile (synthetic replay). Results are attached (bench-results-rc1.csv). Key excerpts below.

--- internal excerpt ---
Environment: Hosted (Redwood rc1) vs Incumbent (MedPrompt-XL v2.1 quant)
Test harness: 60 min mixed-replay, steady concurrency 80, burst run at 220 for 20 min
Payload: chat messages avg 45 tokens, streaming enabled for chat

Results (observed end-to-end client times, median of several runs):
- Redwood rc1 (hosted): p50 60 ms, p95 170 ms, p99 540 ms (steady); burst p95 190 ms, p99 610 ms
- Incumbent: p50 85 ms, p95 240 ms, p99 880 ms (steady); burst p95 310 ms, p99 1,250 ms

Notes:
- Streaming first-partial for rc1: ~110 ms median, 95th ~210 ms under steady load; during burst first-partial 95th ~260 ms
- Cold-start runs (24 hr idle): rc1 p95 inflated ~30–50% on first requests until caches warmed
- KV cache helps more for repeated clinical prompts due to template reuse; quantization of incumbent seems to cause higher tail under burst

Attaching the CSV with raw samples. This is an internal micro-probe (not yet full POC). We used the same replay profile you described.

-marcus

---

Elena — thanks for confirming and for the flexibility on partial timings. Based on Marcus’ preliminary probes I updated the acceptance thresholds in the worksheet to reflect a tight but realistic bar for the POC:

Updated acceptance (POC):
- p95 <= 180 ms (single-turn steady) — aligns with our rc1 steady results
- p99 <= 650 ms (mixed steady/burst) — gives headroom for burst tails, still materially better than incumbent micro-probe
- Streaming first-partial: 95% <= 210 ms (we’ll list 200 ms as target; report real observed values)

Next steps (concrete):
1) Novara to drop 48-hour replay to s3://redwood-uploads/novara/replay-20261203 (ProcureOps)
2) Redwood to run parallel hosted vs incumbent replay runs (we’ll push raw traces and the CSV to the shared Drive link)
3) Review initial report within 7 business days; decide on canary rollout thresholds and any additional run-conditioning (longer bursts / different concurrency shapes)
